title: Polynomial presentations, ideals and conormal modules under field extension
statement:
Let $k\to K$ be a homomorphism of fields, $n\geq0$, $P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $P_K=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $\alpha:P\twoheadrightarrow S$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative $k$-algebras. Put $I=\ker\alpha$, let $\rho:P\to P_K$ apply the field homomorphism to coefficients, and let $I_K$ be the ideal generated by $\rho(I)$. Put $S_K=S\otimes_kK$, with $K$-algebra structure $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$, and $j(s)=s\otimes1$. Tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then the map $\mu:P\otimes_kK\to P_K$, $p\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\rho(p)$, is an isomorphism of $K$-algebras. Its restrictions induce isomorphisms $I\otimes_kK\cong I_K$ and $I^2\otimes_kK\cong I_K^2$, and these commute with the inclusions of the squares into the ideals and the ideals into the polynomial rings. The map $\alpha_K:P_K\to S_K$, $x_i\mapsto\alpha(x_i)\otimes1$, is surjective with kernel $I_K$, satisfies $\alpha_K\rho=j\alpha$, and induces $P_K/I_K\cong S_K$ as $K$-algebras; in particular $S_K$ is finite type over $K$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. The $S$-module $M=I/I^2$ is finitely generated. Writing $M_K=I_K/I_K^2$ as an $S_K$-module through $\alpha_K$, the canonical map
$$\Theta:M\otimes_SS_K\longrightarrow M_K,\qquad (f\bmod I^2)\otimes(s\otimes\lambda)\longmapsto\lambda\rho(pf)\bmod I_K^2\quad(\alpha(p)=s),$$
is well-defined and an $S_K$-linear isomorphism. Under $M\otimes_SS_K\cong M\otimes_kK$, $m\otimes(s\otimes\lambda)\mapsto sm\otimes\lambda$, it is the quotient of the preceding compatible ideal-and-square isomorphisms.

proof.text:
By the polynomial and tensor universal properties, $\mu(p\otimes\lambda)=\lambdaho(p)$ is a $K$-algebra homomorphism. An explicit inverse is $
u(\sum_a\lambda_a x^a)=\sum_a x^a\otimes\lambda_a$. Additivity is coefficientwise, and multiplicativity follows from $(x^a\otimes\lambda)(x^b\otimes\eta)=x^{a+b}\otimes\lambda\eta$. For $p=\sum_a c_a x^a$, balancing gives $\sum_a x^a\otimes\lambda\iota(c_a)=p\otimes\lambda$, where $\iota:k	o K$ is the given map. Thus $
u\mu$ is the identity on pure tensors, and $\mu
u$ is the identity coefficientwise.

source.place: Tag 00S4, lemma-change-base-NL, proof; Tag 00SJ, lemma-lci-field-change, induced presentation and converse conormal comparison. Explicit representative calculation by Q27.

proof.text: For any ideal $J\subseteq P$, apply flatness of $K$ over $k$ and exactness of tensoring to the inclusion $0\to J\to P$. Its tensor followed by $\mu$ is injective. Its image consists of the finite sums $\sum_l\lambda_l\rho(f_l)$ with $f_l\in J$. This is an ideal of $P_K$: multiply such a sum by $\sum_a\eta_a\rho(x^a)$ to obtain $\sum_{a,l}\eta_a\lambda_l\rho(x^a f_l)$, with $x^a f_l\in J$. It contains $\rho(J)$, and each of its terms belongs to the ideal generated by $\rho(J)$, so it is exactly that ideal. Take $J=I$ and $J=I^2$. The extended ideal of $I^2$ equals $I_K^2$: products $\rho(f)\rho(g)=\rho(fg)$ generate the square in one direction, and every element of $I^2$ is a finite sum of products of elements of $I$ in the other. Hence the two injective maps identify $I\otimes_kK$ with $I_K$ and $I^2\otimes_kK$ with $I_K^2$. Both are restrictions of $\mu$; therefore their inclusion squares commute.

source.place: Tags 00HB/00HD (definition-flat, lemma-flat), applied to vector spaces; Tag 00S4 (lemma-change-base-NL), proof. Ideal and square image calculation written explicitly.

proof.text: Define $\alpha_K$ by evaluation at $\alpha(x_i)\otimes1$. The two $k$-algebra maps $\alpha_K\rho$ and $j\alpha$ agree on every variable and on constants, so are equal. Consequently $\alpha_K\mu(p\otimes\lambda)=\alpha(p)\otimes\lambda$. Tensor the exact sequences $0\to I\to P\xrightarrow{\alpha}S$ and $P\xrightarrow{\alpha}S\to0$ with the flat $k$-module $K$. They show that $\alpha_K$ is surjective and that its kernel is the image of $I\otimes_kK$, namely $I_K$ by step 2. The map $\bar q\mapsto\alpha_K(q)$ from $P_K/I_K$ is thus well-defined and injective (its zero classes are exactly $I_K$), and surjective; its inverse sends $z$ to the class of any preimage. This is a $K$-algebra isomorphism. The displayed surjection from the finite-variable polynomial ring makes $S_K$ finite type.

source.place: Tag 00S4, lemma-change-base-NL, proof; Tag 00SJ, lemma-lci-field-change, induced presentation and converse conormal comparison. Explicit representative calculation by Q27.

proof.text: The polynomial-ring regularity statement includes that $P$ is Noetherian. The $P$-module $P$ is generated by $1$, so its submodule $I$ is finitely generated. Choose generators $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ of $I$. Their classes generate $M=I/I^2$ over $S$: an expression $f=\sum_i p_i f_i$ descends to $[f]=\sum_i\alpha(p_i)[f_i]$. This also explicitly defines the $S$-action: $s[f]=[pf]$ for any lift $\alpha(p)=s$, independently of the lift since $(p-p')f\in I^2$. Thus no finite-dimensionality over $k$ is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 00OQ (proposition-finite-gl-dim-polynomial-ring), first sentence; Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), second assertion; quotient generator calculation.

proof.text: Tensor $I^2\to I\to M\to0$ with $K$. Flatness and exactness identify $M\otimes_kK$ with the cokernel of $I^2\otimes_kK\to I\otimes_kK$: the quotient map is surjective and its kernel is the image of the square. Under the compatible isomorphisms of step 2, that image is exactly $I_K^2\subseteq I_K$. Taking quotients therefore gives a $K$-linear isomorphism $e:M\otimes_kK\to I_K/I_K^2$ characterized by $e([f]\otimes\lambda)=[\lambda\rho(f)]$. Concretely, the inverse takes a finite sum $\sum_l\lambda_l\rho(f_l)$ to $\sum_l[f_l]\otimes\lambda_l$; independence of the expression follows from injectivity of $I\otimes_kK\to P_K$, and changing the representative by $I_K^2$ gives zero by the just-proved exactness.

source.place: Tag 00S4, lemma-change-base-NL, proof; Tag 00SJ, lemma-lci-field-change, induced presentation and converse conormal comparison. Explicit representative calculation by Q27.

proof.text: The tensor universal property gives $\gamma:M\otimes_S(S\otimes_kK)\to M\otimes_kK$, $m\otimes(s\otimes\lambda)\mapsto sm\otimes\lambda$. Its inverse is $\delta(m\otimes\lambda)=m\otimes(1\otimes\lambda)$: these formulas respect the $k$- and $S$-balancing relations, and $sm\otimes(1\otimes\lambda)=m\otimes(s\otimes\lambda)$ proves both composites are the identity on generators. The $S_K$-action on $M\otimes_kK$ is $(s\otimes\eta)(m\otimes\lambda)=sm\otimes\eta\lambda$, so $\gamma$ is $S_K$-linear. This argument works for any $S$-module, including the zero module.

source.place: Tag 00S4, lemma-change-base-NL, proof; Tag 00SJ, lemma-lci-field-change, induced presentation and converse conormal comparison. Explicit representative calculation by Q27.

proof.text: Put $\Theta=e\gamma$. For $f\in I$, $s\in S$, $\lambda\in K$, choose $p\in P$ with $\alpha(p)=s$. Step 4 and the formula for $e$ give $\Theta([f]\otimes(s\otimes\lambda))=[\lambda\rho(pf)]$, as required. Changing $p$ by an element of $I$, or $f$ by an element of $I^2$, changes this output by an element of $I_K^2$. To verify the stronger scalar linearity of $e$, write $s=\alpha(p)$ and compute $e((s\otimes\eta)([f]\otimes\lambda))=[\eta\lambda\rho(pf)]=(s\otimes\eta)e([f]\otimes\lambda)$, where the target action uses $P_K/I_K\cong S_K$ from step 3. Additivity and generation by pure tensors extend this equality to all scalars and vectors. Hence $e$ and $\Theta$ are $S_K$-linear bijections, and step 5 proves the final assertion that this is the quotient of the compatible ideal-and-square comparisons.
